summary: This joint resolution blocks the proposed sale to Israel of 201 MK 83 bomb bodies, 4,799 BLU-110A/B bomb bodies, and 5,000 related JDAM guidance kits that were notified to Congress in Transmittal No. 25-26.

scores.thoughts: The bill blocks a specific arms export sale but does not alter any US government budget outlays, appropriations, or domestic spending levels. Arms sales under the Arms Export Control Act are typically funded by the foreign purchaser, so there is no direct impact on US spending.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
The legislation concerns only a proposed arms sale and has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
The bill addresses 1,000-pound bombs and JDAM kits, not firearms or domestic gun regulations.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the text.
The resolution contains nothing related to reproductive health or abortion access.

While the bill blocks export of US-origin munitions, it does not change US defense budget levels, procurement for US forces, or overall military spending. The transaction is a foreign sale, not an appropriation.
No environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions are present.
The measure does not touch welfare programs, entitlements, or social spending.
No education funding, school policy, or student-aid language exists.
The bill is silent on controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
No criminal sentencing, policing, or justice-system reforms are addressed.

The resolution blocks one discrete arms export but does not establish tariffs, trade agreements, or broad protectionist measures; it is a targeted foreign-policy action under existing export-control law.
No deficit, debt-ceiling, or fiscal-balance provisions are included.
The text contains no civil-rights or LGBTQ-related content.

The joint resolution explicitly prohibits a proposed foreign military sale of munitions to Israel. Although structured as a commercial sale rather than grant aid, disapproving the transfer directly reduces US military support provided to a foreign country, aligning with the 'reduce or eliminate foreign aid' direction.
No voting, election administration, or campaign-finance provisions exist.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data, or privacy standards.
No labor, union, or employment-law content is present.
The resolution addresses only an arms sale and contains no religious-exemption or civil-rights language.
